title: Pilot study comparing the efficacy of intra-articular glenohumeral injection combined with suprascapular nerve block versus intra-articular glenohumeral corticosteroid injection in adhesive capsulitis.
official: Pilot study comparing the efficacy of intra-articular glenohumeral injection combined with suprascapular nerve block versus intra-articular glenohumeral corticosteroid injection in adhesive capsulitis.
summary: Main objective: Compare the improvement in shoulder function at 3 months between the intra-articular injection group combined with a suprascapular nerve block and the intra-articular injection group combined with a placebo block.

interventions.name: DIPROSTENE, suspension injectable en seringue pré-remplie

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Patients with shoulder stiffness lasting at least 2 months and less than 12 months, with a loss of passive joint range of motion in at least 2 planes (lateral rotation, medial rotation, abduction, antepulsion) of at least 30 degrees compared to the contralateral side
2. Patients aged between 18 and 65 years
3. Patients affiliated with a social security system
Exclusion criteria:
1. Corticosteroid injection in the affected shoulder < 4 months
2. - Anticoagulation with VKA or anti-Xa, or bleeding disorder currently active or in remission for less than 5 years (malignant blood disorders, myelodysplasia, autoimmune thrombocytopenia) or chemotherapy (antiplatelet agents authorized except prasugrel and clopidogrel)*
3. Uncontrolled high blood pressure,
4. Uncontrolled diabetes or at risk of decompensation,
5. Contraindications for diprosten, Kenacort, or lidocaine
6. Persons belonging to a vulnerable group as defined by Regulation (EU) No. 536/2014 and French law
7. Patients who are unable to comply with the protocol requirements
8. Psychiatric condition likely to be decompensated by corticosteroids
9. Women who are pregnant or breastfeeding or who refuse effective contraception
10. Patients participating in another clinical research protocol involving a drug or medical device
11. Patients refusing to participate in the study
12. History of any surgery on the affected shoulder within the last 12 months
13. Patients with neuromuscular disorders (neurological deficits) or shoulder disorders (arthropathy) that could interfere with the assessment of the primary endpoint
14. Signs or risks of infection (bacterial infection and/or fever and/or antibiotic use)
15. Poor skin condition of the pathological shoulder
